idiom_name: kotlinx.html DSL fragments composed as functions (Ktor respondHtml / respondHtmlFragment)
implementation_notes: Kotlin expresses the pattern as ordinary function composition over a typed HTML DSL: a fragment is an extension function on the DSL receiver (fun FlowContent.productRow(p: Product)) and the page is createHTML().html { layout(title) { productList(products) } }, so a placeholder is a function call, fragments take typed parameters, and there is no include mechanism to configure. Ktor renders that builder with call.respondHtml { ... } and (from Ktor 3.4) call.respondHtmlFragment { ... } for HTMX-style partial responses that reuse the same fragment functions; Spring Boot stacks instead compose Thymeleaf th:replace fragments over template files. Choose the DSL form when markup is code and type safety matters, Thymeleaf when designers own templates.
pitfalls: kotlinx.html writes through a consumer: fragments must emit inside the DSL block - building a String separately and injecting it with unsafe { } bypasses escaping and reintroduces injection risk.
respondHtml sends a full document while respondHtmlFragment sends no <html>/<head>/<body> wrapper, so fragment functions designed for full pages cannot be reused unchanged in an HTMX endpoint.

Because fragments are plain functions, forgetting the receiver (FlowContent) or the DSL scope silently attaches markup in the wrong place; tests against the rendered string catch what the type system does not.
